children: Macquarie's new chief executive is likely to increase the Australian financial group's focus on costs, UBS analysts reckon. Greg Ward is scheduled to succeed Shemara Wikramanayake next week, and the UBS analysts expect him to look at potential cost reductions. Forward-looking guidance will be key to assessing the likely timing of any targeted efficiencies, they tell clients in a note. They point out that Macquarie's 65% cost-to-income ratio remains high compared with peers, and think a 4 percentage-point reduction could add about 570 million Australian dollars to annual cash earnings. UBS maintains a neutral rating and A$265.00 target price on the stock, which is up 1.0% at A$251.72. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
